To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) We introduce TrueLearn, a set of online algorithms for recommending open educational resources that account for both the novelty and background of the learner, 2) We propose a set of novel Bayesian models for knowledge state tracking, and 3) We evaluate the proposed algorithms on an educational video dataset, and show that our approach outperforms a state-of-the-art recommendation algorithm.
we propose a set of Bayesian algorithms to match learners with educational resources based on their knowledge state, and that the performance of our algorithms is promising.
the proposed algorithms, TrueLearn, outperform the state-of-the-art in the educational recommendation literature, with the TrueLearn-3 algorithm performing best.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and evaluation of a set of online algorithms for recommending educational resources to lifelong learners.

developing a scalable, transparent and dynamic recommendation system for lifelong learning, and the proposed algorithms are the first step in this direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

TrueLearn is a family of Bayesian algorithms that can be used to match lifelong learners to open educational resources, based on their background knowledge, the novelty of the material and their engagement with the material.

we present a set of algorithms that are able to recommend open educational resources that match learners' backgrounds, and are able to maintain the knowledge state of learners over a long period of time, and that these algorithms are able to do so with high accuracy.
TrueLearn is an open, scalable, transparent, and effective recommendation model for educational resources that can be used for building a lifelong learning recommendation systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a family of online Bayesian algorithms for matching learners with open educational resources and evaluate them using a dataset of over 100,000 learners and 10,000 videos.

the TrueLearn algorithms provide a set of tools to build an educational recommendation system for lifelong learners, which is scalable, transparent, dynamic and effective in recommending open educational resources to a large population of learners.
we present a novel approach to lifelong learning recommendation systems by proposing a family of Bayesian algorithms, which we call TrueLearn, to match learners to open educational resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a lifelong learning recommendation model can be built from implicit data and can be used to improve learner engagement.
the proposed algorithms are effective at recommending educational content to lifelong learners, which opens the door for building scalable and cost-effective lifelong learning systems.

the proposed algorithms can be used in a variety of educational settings, and can be easily extended to other domains, e.g., news articles, movies, and books, to build lifelong learning recommendation systems for those domains as well.
